request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

transcript (39 turns):
[0] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Okay, I think we've got everyone. Tom, you there? Brian's on, Ananya's on — Sofia, can you confirm?
[1] Sofia Petrov (aegis_staff): Yeah I'm here, sorry, I was just pulling up the dashboards.
[2] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Good. Okay, let's not waste time. Tom, do you want to kick us off or should I?
[3] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): I'll start. So, uh, at approximately 9:14 AM Pacific we started seeing alerts — or rather, the absence of alerts — from the Detect event processing pipeline. The ingestion layer just... stopped. No events coming through, no throughput, and the monitoring didn't catch it immediately which is its own problem we're going to talk about.
[4] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): When you say the monitoring didn't catch it — are we talking about our internal alerting or the customer-facing status stuff?
[5] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Both, honestly. Internal alerting had a lag, and the status page wasn't updated until... Ananya, when did we actually post to the status page?
[6] Ananya Sharma (aegis_staff): It was around 10:40, so that's — yeah, that's about an hour and a half after the initial failure. And I want to be upfront, that's on me partly because I was the one who was supposed to pull the trigger on that and I was heads-down trying to figure out the root cause first.
[7] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Ananya, I appreciate you saying that but that's a process failure, not a you failure. We shouldn't have a single person making the call on when to post. That's a systemic issue.
[8] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): I mean — I agree with that, but we can talk process later. Right now I've got customers blowing up my team's queue and I need to understand what actually happened technically so I can give my support engineers something to say.
[9] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Right, yeah. Sofia, you want to walk through the technical failure? You were in the weeds on this from the start.
[10] Sofia Petrov (aegis_staff): Sure. So the event ingestion pipeline — basically it's a single primary node that handles all incoming threat event data before it fans out to the processing workers. That node hit a memory ceiling, started throwing OOM errors, and because we don't have a circuit breaker or any redundancy on that node, it just cascaded. Everything downstream starved out.
[11] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Wait, so there's literally one node doing all of the ingestion? That's... okay I'm not an engineer but that sounds like a really bad design.
[12] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): It's not ideal, no. It's — look, it's a legacy architecture decision and it's been on the roadmap to address. We just hadn't prioritized it.
[13] Ananya Sharma (aegis_staff): It was flagged in the Q4 tech debt review, Tom. I flagged it.
[14] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): I know you did. And I'm not — look, this is not the time for that conversation. Yes, it was flagged, yes, it should have been prioritized, and now we're dealing with the consequences. I own that.
[15] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Okay. So what's the current status? Are customers seeing data right now or are we still down?
[16] Ananya Sharma (aegis_staff): We're still down as of this call. Sofia and I have been working on a hotfix — we're spinning up a secondary ingestion node and routing traffic through a temporary load balancer config, but it's not clean. It's a stopgap.
[17] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): How long until that stopgap is live?
[18] Sofia Petrov (aegis_staff): Best case? Another hour, maybe ninety minutes. But I don't want to commit to that publicly yet.
[19] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Brian, what are you hearing from customers? Like, who's screaming the loudest right now?
[20] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): I mean, everyone in the enterprise tier is screaming. We've got — let me just look at my notes here — Harmon Financial has escalated twice, they're threatening to call their account manager directly. TerraLogix is asking whether this is a breach, which is a great question to get at 10 in the morning. And we've got at least a dozen mid-market customers who are just, you know, sitting there with a broken security product and no visibility into their threat environment.
[21] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): TerraLogix thinks it's a breach? We need to get ahead of that immediately.
[22] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): I know, I've got one of my senior support reps on the phone with them right now. But Tom, I need an actual statement I can give customers about what happened. Something honest that doesn't make us look like we don't know what we're doing.
[23] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): The problem is we're still root-causing. I don't want to put out a statement that's wrong.
[24] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Tom, we know enough. It's a pipeline failure. It's not a breach. That's the most important thing to communicate right now. Customers would rather have an incomplete honest update than silence.
[25] Ananya Sharma (aegis_staff): I agree with Brian on this one. We've been in communications blackout for too long already.
[26] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Fine. Fine. I'll draft something in the next — can someone give me fifteen minutes and I'll have a customer statement?
[27] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Please. And make sure it explicitly says this is not a security breach, that's the first question everyone's asking.
[28] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Yeah, I will. Sofia, while I'm doing that — can you document what you know so far about the failure sequence? We're going to need a timeline for the post-mortem.
[29] Sofia Petrov (aegis_staff): Already started. I've got a doc in Confluence, I'll drop the link in Slack. One thing I want to flag though — when we bring the stopgap online, customers are going to start seeing alerts again but there may be a gap in their event history. Like, events that occurred during the outage window may not be recoverable. We need to be upfront about that.
[30] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Oh, that's — yeah, that's going to be a very bad conversation to have with customers in regulated industries. Are we sure about that? Is there any way to replay the events?
[31] Ananya Sharma (aegis_staff): We have some buffering at the source layer but it's limited. I'd say we can recover maybe sixty to seventy percent of what was lost. The rest is... gone.
[32] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Okay. That's — we need to think carefully about how we communicate that. That's a significant data loss event for a security monitoring product.
[33] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Agreed. Let's not bury it. Put it in the post-incident report. Customers deserve to know.
[34] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Can we talk about the immediate next steps? I just want to make sure we have a clear owner on each thing before we get off this call, because the last two hours have been a lot of people doing a lot of things without coordination.
[35] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Yes. Okay. Sofia and Ananya, you own the stopgap fix and the technical timeline doc. Brian, you own customer communications and escalation triage. I'll draft the public statement and then I'm going to get on a call with the CTO because she's going to need to know about this if she doesn't already.
[36] Ananya Sharma (aegis_staff): She knows. I got a Slack from her about forty minutes ago.
[37] Tom Bradley (aegis_staff): Great. That's... great. Okay. Let's reconvene in ninety minutes or sooner if the fix goes live. Everybody check in on Slack. And — I know this has been a rough morning. Let's just get it fixed.
[38] Brian Cho (aegis_staff): Agreed. Let's go.
